pr_title: Fix all possible setting error related storages and added some tests
pr_body:
Follow up #22405

Fix #20703 

This PR rewrites storage configuration read sequences with some breaks and tests. It becomes more strict than before and also fixed some inherit problems.

- Move storage's MinioConfig struct into setting, so after the configuration loading, the values will be stored into the struct but not still on some section.
- Add more tests for storages configurations.
- Update the storage documentations.

The break changes

- All storages configurations should be stored in one section, configuration items cannot be overrided by multiple  sections now. The priority of configuration is `[attachment]` > `[storage.attachments]` |  `[storage.customized]` > `[storage]` > `default`
- For extra override configuration items, currently are `SERVE_DIRECT`, `MINIO_BASE_PATH`, `MINIO_BUCKET`, which could be configured in another section. The prioioty of the override configuration is `[attachment]` > `[storage.attachments]` > `default`.

i.e. This is a previous supported configuration
```ini
[storage]
STOTRAGE_TYPE = minio
MINIO_LOCATION = euro
MINIO_USE_SSL = false

[storage.lfs]
MINIO_BUCKET = my_bucket

[lfs]
MINIO_BASE_PATH = lfs/
```

Now it will not be supported. Only one section can be derived. You need to change it like below.
```ini
[storage]
STOTRAGE_TYPE = minio
MINIO_LOCATION = euro
MINIO_USE_SSL = false

[storage.lfs]
MINIO_BUCKET = my_bucket
MINIO_BASE_PATH = lfs/

[lfs]
```

or 

```ini
[storage]
STOTRAGE_TYPE = minio
MINIO_LOCATION = euro
MINIO_USE_SSL = false

[lfs]
MINIO_BUCKET = my_bucket
MINIO_BASE_PATH = lfs/
```

And below will not be allowed because `MINIO_USE_SSL` cannot be as a derived item. Only `SERVE_DIRECT`, `MINIO_BASE_PATH`, `MINIO_BUCKET` can be derived items.

```ini
[storage]
STOTRAGE_TYPE = minio
MINIO_LOCATION = euro

[lfs]
MINIO_USE_SSL = false
MINIO_BUCKET = my_bucket
MINIO_BASE_PATH = lfs/
```

issue_context.title: The storage.repo-archive and storage.packages configs do not accept custom STORAGE_TYPE
issue_context.body:
### Description

Hello,

I am using S3 storage provided by my Ceph cluster for Gitea's LFS, Avatar, attachment, repo-archive and packages storage. My storage configuration currently looks like this:

```
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
[storage]
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
STORAGE_TYPE = my_minio

[lfs]
STORAGE_TYPE = my_minio

;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
[storage.repo-archive]
;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;
STORAGE_TYPE            = minio
MINIO_ENDPOINT          = s3.my-domain.net
MINIO_BUCKET            = gitea
MINIO_LOCATION          = homenet
MINIO_USE_SSL           = true
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID     = correct_key
MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = correct_key

[storage.packages]
STORAGE_TYPE            = minio
MINIO_ENDPOINT          = s3.mei-home.net:7481
MINIO_BUCKET            = gitea
MINIO_LOCATION          = homenet
MINIO_USE_SSL           = true
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID     = correct_key
MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = correct_key

[storage.my_minio]
STORAGE_TYPE            = minio
MINIO_ENDPOINT          = s3.my-domain.net
MINIO_BUCKET            = gitea
MINIO_LOCATION          = homenet
MINIO_USE_SSL           = true
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID     = correct_key
MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = correct_key
```
This configuration works without problems. But I need to repeat my S3 configuration three times. Once for the default storage config used by attachments and so on, and then once each for the package and repo-archive storage.

Now to the bug itself. I had originally hoped that the two new storage items, packages and repo-archive would work similar to the `lfs` section above, by only setting the `STORAGE_TYPE` option to `my_minio`, avoiding the multiple repeats of the S3 configs.
But with the following config, I'm getting errors during Gitea startup:
```

; storage type

MINIO_LOCATION          = homenet
MINIO_USE_SSL           = true
MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID     = correct_key
MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = correct_key

review_comments:
It can't be simply removed.

For example, a user from old instance have `LFS_CONTENT_PATH` in its config.

If you remove it, and Gitea starts, the LFS storage is not initialized correctly, then the LFS files are lost?

It needs to have a "fatal" error to force users to update their config.

```
[storage]
STORAGE_TYPE = minio
[storage.sub]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
```

This `SetValue` will overwrite STORAGE_TYPE in `[storage]` section.
Because targetSec's STORAGE_TYPE is empty, so we can do it safely. See line 125-127

```
[storage]
STORAGE_TYPE = minio
[storage.sub1]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
[storage.sub2]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
```

Then if you overwrite the `STORAGE_TYPE` for `[storage.sub1]`, it also affects `[storage.sub2]`, is it intentional?

No. It will not affect sub2. This logic will help to fill the storage type for this situation when `PATH` is not empty, then we will set `STORAGE_TYPE` to `local`.

```ini
[storage.lfs]
PATH =
```

Suppose: 

```
[storage]
STORAGE_TYPE = minio
[storage.sub1]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
[storage.sub2]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
```

Then `targetSec.Key("STORAGE_TYPE")` points to `[storage].STORAGE_TYPE`, then you set it to "local"

Now the INI becomes:

```
[storage]
STORAGE_TYPE = local
[storage.sub1]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
[storage.sub2]
; no STORAGE_TYPE
```


I still do not think it is right.
The updating will be triggered only when `STORAGE_TYPE` is empty and `PATH` is not empty. In your example, STORAGE_TYPE is not empty.

Hmm, maybe my example is not appropriate. But I can see using `Key` + `SetValue` in sub section is fragile and maybe even dangerous. Hopefully no user would be affected by it. Fortunately, it could be bypassed by writing everything explicitly.
